title: bn254-pairing-inversion: tag-tracing 8-adding distinguished-point rho in GT, output (P0,[x]Q0)

claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial algorithm in proof.md (an 8-adding Pollard-rho walk Y -> Y*M_s in GT with s=floor(8t/p) for the protected-basis constant coefficient t of Y, evaluated by tag tracing: a certified 64-bit inner-product approximation of t against a precomputed table of all products of at most 256 multipliers, one Fp12 product per 256 steps, exact evaluation whenever the certificate fails; distinguished points of density 2^-80; at most S=floor(sqrt(1409*r/1000))+1 steps in total; scalar recovery and verification g^x=z) returns P0 and [x]Q0 with e(P0,[x]Q0)=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.39, using at most 2^121.285447 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) and less than 2^60 bytes of peak total storage. The instruction bound, valid for every run including all failures, is 273*S + 24576*(floor(S/256)+1) + 2^110, derived in machine.md from the supplied listings ttstep.disasm.txt (273 executed instructions per certified step) and tower.disasm.txt (24,132 per window re-base) and from metered caps on all other work, including construction of the 525,783,425,977,953-entry table for this one target. The tag certificate (proof.md section 2) and the degeneracy probability 1/r are proved; the success assessment relies on the disclosed heuristics H1 (8-adding collision law with correction 8/7, model value 0.4601 at the cap) and H2 (uniformity of tag bits), supported and limited as explained in proof.md and by the toy-scale experiments; it is not an unconditional production success theorem, an index-calculus attack or a security estimate. No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or production-scale execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: At full BN254 width: check the tower formulas against the protected basis, the tag row identity, the tag certificate interval on random and edge cases, and a 120-step walk through the real solve loop (exact selector, one multiplier per step, label invariant, identical walk under forced exact evaluations). Run the complete algorithm with the production cap formula on toy prime-field subgroups, reporting all outcomes including failures. Recount the executed instructions from the two supplied listings and recompute the capped cost. These do not prove production success.
